note: Hand-verified attestation. Every record here was confirmed by READING the cited write-up, not by matching a keyword. Merged with the auto-seeded records into v3/evidence.json by `v3/build_evidence.py`; a curated record wins over a seeded one for the same technique.
method: Candidates came from the local base github.com/blue101010/ctf, restricted to files that repository actually tracks (94 of 152 markdown write-ups) and matched on prose only — fenced code, JSON dumps and certificate blobs excluded. Every surviving candidate was then read. Rejections are recorded below so they are not re-proposed.

challenges.extracted_from: read and confirmed: sha256crypt hash extracted from an embedded device, hashcat -m 7400 against rockyou, then a rule-based pass
read and confirmed: Kerberoast TGS-REP hash, hashcat -m 13100 against seclists, Status: Cracked

positives: the challenge yields a hash in a documented format and the flag is the plaintext behind it (sha256crypt $5$, Kerberos 5 TGS-REP etype 23)
the constraint is the candidate space, not the algorithm: mode selection plus the right wordlist or rule set is the whole solve
a rule pass (best64) or a themed wordlist succeeds where a plain wordlist exhausts
negatives: online credential brute-force against a login form (hydra against http-post-form) — no hash is ever recovered, the oracle is the application
a hash whose plaintext is irrelevant because the challenge only needs the hash as an identifier
recovering a key by exploiting the cipher's structure rather than by search — that is CTFTTE-CRY-001 or CTFTTE-CRY-003
boundaries: distinct from CTFTTE-CRY-001 (weak RSA parameters): there the key falls to arithmetic, here only to search
distinct from CTFTTE-CRY-004 (nonce reuse): no cryptanalytic relation is exploited
online brute-force is NOT this technique and has no CTFT entry yet — see the candidate list in TODO.md

external_mappings.justification: Password Cracking is the exact ATT&CK behaviour; CTFT adds the mode-selection and wordlist-constraint craft ATT&CK omits.
Use of a password hash with insufficient computational effort is what makes the search tractable.

challenges.extracted_from: read and confirmed: a single PCAP carries five questions; the asset naming convention and the target hostname are recovered from the scan traffic
read and confirmed: tshark -r capture.pcap --export-objects http reassembles the transferred objects that carry the flag

positives: the payload exists only as a reassembled stream or exported object, never in a single packet
the capture is legitimate traffic and the concealment is dilution: the answer is one conversation among many
the solve is a reassembly and export operation, not a decode of one field
negatives: a flag readable in a single packet payload with `strings` — no reassembly is required
a link to a packet-capture resource or a mention of pcap tooling in a threat-intel note — describing the format is not exercising the technique
a covert channel in protocol header fields, which is CTFTTE-NET-006
boundaries: distinct from CTFTTE-NET-007 (packet-capture forensics maze): NET frames the network puzzle, FOR frames artifact reassembly from the capture
distinct from CTFTTE-NET-002 (DNS covert channel): there the carrier is the protocol, here the carrier is the stream
distinct from CTFTTE-STE-002 (appended data): the container is a capture, not a file with trailing bytes

external_mappings.justification: Application Layer Protocol is the carrier ATT&CK models; ATT&CK omits the reassembly and export craft that defines the CTF technique.

rejected.reason: the `unpack` match is `bag_unpack(ASRConfig)`, a KQL function in a hunting query — nothing is unpacked
the `unpack` match is dpkg output (`Preparing to unpack libreadline-dev.deb`)
a real Privilege Escalation section, but Active Directory (ldapsearch, UserAccountControl) — that attests CTFTTE-FPN-002, not the Linux SUID/sudo chain
describes REMCOS malware features including privilege escalation; the solver never escalates
hydra against an http-post-form login — online brute-force, no hash is recovered; a different behaviour that CTFT does not yet declare
the pcap mention is a link to malware-traffic-analysis.net, not a capture the author analysed

rejected.technique: CTFTTE-CRY-001 / CRY-003 / CRY-008 / PWN-004 / REV-005 / WEB-010 / OSI-008
rejected.reason: one 15 KB threat-intel note containing a Shodan JSON dump; RSA, ROP, Z3 and padding-oracle all matched inside an embedded TLS certificate (sha256WithRSAEncryption, ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20). Attests none of them

rejected.technique: candidate CRY entry for ECDSA / elliptic curve
rejected.reason: every match is an nmap ssh-hostkey banner line (`256 ... (ECDSA)`). No elliptic-curve cryptanalysis anywhere in the base — the gap is real but has zero local evidence, so no entry was created
